title: What sends traffic to Cloud Browser: Internet & SaaS rules, Smart Isolation and the Private Access isolation policy

prose.text: Zero Trust Browser has no policy engine of its own in the captured sources: other products' rules send traffic to it, each naming an isolation profile. {{enable-prereqs}} {{policy-steps}}

URL Filtering's Isolate action: [[zia.url-filtering.actions:isolate-needs-zbi]], with the provider's checks on such a rule in [[zia.terraform.url-filtering-rules:isolate-validation]]. Cloud App Control's Isolate actions and their restriction: [[zia.cloud-app-control.actions:console-actions]], [[zia.cloud-app-control.actions:isolate-not-mixed]]. The Device Groups criterion has a Cloud Browser Isolation choice: [[zia.iot.policy-use:iot-device-group]].
AI/ML-driven isolation of suspicious sites is in [[zbi.smart-isolation]]. Whether a manual Isolate rule needs SSL/TLS inspection on HTTPS is partly answered {{gap:manual-isolate-ssl}}.
Private application requests are sent to isolation by the isolation policy, which also needs an access policy: [[zbi.private-access-isolation]].

The profile objects every rule names are in [[zbi.isolation-profiles]]; a tenant whose subscription covers only the Miscellaneous & Unknown category gets a fixed profile and rule, in [[zbi.misc-unknown-subscription]].

checks.do: Whether Cloud Browser is enabled for the organization and an isolation profile exists for the rule to name.
Whether HTTPS traffic meant for isolation is decrypted, or matched a Do Not Inspect rule first.

enable-prereqs.statement: The Cloud Browser configuration guide's prerequisites are access to an Internet & SaaS or Private Access tenant, a Zero Trust Browser subscription, supporting Private Access infrastructure such as App Connector, and an identity provider with conditional access capabilities; Cloud Browser is enabled for an organization by contacting Zscaler Support.

quotes: Access to an Internet & SaaS or a Private Access tenant.
A subscription to Zero Trust Browser.
Supporting Private Access infrastructure (e.g., App Connector or Application Access).
An identity provider (IdP) with conditional access capabilities (e.g., IP restrictions or context-aware policy).
Contact Zscaler Support to get Cloud Browser enabled for your organization.

policy-steps.statement: After creating isolation profiles, the guide maps policies to them: for Internet & SaaS, configuring Internet & SaaS for Cloud Browser, the Cloud App Control policy, the Smart Browser Isolation policy and the Sandbox integration; for Private Access, learning about the isolation policy, configuring isolation policies, the access policy for Cloud Browser and secure SaaS access from unmanaged devices through the User Portal.

quotes: Configure policies to map to the isolation profiles:
Configure Internet & SaaS for Cloud Browser.
Configure the cloud app control policy.
Configure the Smart Browser Isolation policy.
Configure the Sandbox integration with Cloud Browser.
Configure the access policy for Cloud Browser.
Configure secure SaaS access from unmanaged devices via the User Portal.

manual-isolate-ssl.title: Whether a manual URL Filtering Isolate rule needs SSL/TLS inspection for HTTPS
manual-isolate-ssl.detail: Smart Browser Isolation decrypts suspicious sites through SSL/TLS Inspection, and the SSL/TLS inspection guide lists Isolation among the features that need decrypted traffic to work on encrypted transactions. No source states what a manual URL Filtering or Cloud App Control Isolate rule does with HTTPS traffic that matched a Do Not Inspect rule: whether the redirect still happens on the domain, or the rule does not fire.
manual-isolate-ssl.blocks: saying whether an Isolate rule failing on HTTPS is caused by an SSL inspection bypass
